title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Yet, Heard', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the lit phone booth: a glass street booth with a steel frame, a folding door, a lit ceiling panel and a steel wall phone; the only warm box on a cold quay (lit, empty, poet inside, palm on glass, dawn, light off); the call (the cord of light): a dashed, pulsed line between two callers: paper-white against the night sky, ink-dark against the dawn; it bows up to the moon for the lover, sags into the water for the mother (crest at the moon (lover), sagging into the abyss (mother), pulled east (father), gone); the moon: a cream paper disc with three small soft maria and a thin grey rim; the brightest thing in the film until the sun (high over the harbour, gone (the dead hour), settling west behind the walkers); the sun in the harbour mouth: only the part of a disc above the waterline: a half sun sitting in the gap of the far shore. No still fits. (sliver, half up); the two suitcases: POET's black hard-shell roller; EX's worn brown leather case; side by side at their feet by the booth. No still fits. (open, zipped, in hand); the father's footprints: a trail of dark worn shoe prints on wet quay stone, about 70 cm stride, pointing east (already there, stepped into); payphone handset: black steel-armoured handset on a steel cord. No still fits. (at the ear, on the hook); the mother's receiver: cream home receiver on a coiled cord, with a cream rotary desk phone. No still fits. (at her ear, in her lap); mother's armchair: upholstered floral armchair. No still fits. (occupied); folded jacket: the poet's black jacket folded over his forearm. No still fits. (over the arm). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
